relevance_note: Post-mortem metabolomic study of one individually described patient with the diagnosis: 'a 37 y.o. male patient with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD)'; no ALDH5A1 variant is printed.
method_note: Single patient (label 'patient', rule 5; 'The patient' is a role word). Eight post-mortem control subjects (Table 1) are not in scope and get no rows; cohort_size_as_stated left null because no patient cohort is stated. No variants row: the paper prints no ALDH5A1 variant and never explicitly ties an ALDH5A1 variant to this patient (only 'differed significantly by genotype'); ALDH5A1 appears only in a reference title. Table 1 transcribed by eye: patient row gives age 37, 'C' (Caucasian per legend), M, cause of death SUDEP, medication Risperidone; height/weight and tissue harvest time not recorded as features. Epilepsy recorded as observed only from the death attribution 'SUDEP (sudden unexpected death of epilepsy)'; no other clinical features are described ('clinical course typical of SSADHD' is not specific). Age 37 used as age at last evaluation (post-mortem at death). Tissue metabolite findings recorded as features with the paper's direction; Table 2 'PM Tissue' row not used separately (same findings). Stacked cells: none. Contradictions in the paper: serine elevated by MassTrak but below control range by filter-paper assay (both rows emitted; paper itself calls the approaches 'sometimes contradictory'); creatine 'decreased' across tissues and 'confirmed in liver and kidney' with liver within control range, yet the Discussion says creatine was significantly elevated in liver and kidney (rows for both emitted); free GABA within control range (MassTrak, no hydrolysis) vs total GABA elevated (different assays, both recorded). Discussion also says aspartic acid was 'decreased' in cortical sections in one sentence, contradicting the elevated aspartic acid reported elsewhere; only the elevated finding was recorded (stated repeatedly), noted here. Built with a short Python script; spans checked verbatim.
